To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the microbial diversity of pollen was correlated with the allergenicity of the pollen and with air pollution.
the microbiota of allergenic pollen was correlated to air pollution parameters and the expression of allergen proteins and pollen-associated lipid mediator compounds.
pollen-associated microbiota correlates with parameters of air pollution and pollen allergenicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the microbiome of pollen grains on their allergenicity.
a better understanding of the role of pollen-associated microbes and their correlation to allergenicity and air pollution.
a better understanding of the pollen-associated microbiome in order to improve the knowledge of the complex interactions of pollen with the environment and the human immune system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the microbial composition on pollen might be a useful parameter for assessing environmental pollution.
the microbial colonization on birch pollen was significantly correlated to air pollution, whereas the microbial colonization on grass pollen was correlated with the allergenicity of the pollen.
environmental and microbial factors can influence the allergenicity of allergenic pollen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the microbial colonization on pollen might be an important factor in allergenicity and should be taken into account when investigating allergenicity of airborne pollen.
the pollen-associated microbiome correlates to environmental parameters and allergen expression.
the pollen microbiome is correlated with air pollution and allergenicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the microbial composition and diversity on pollen are correlated to air pollution and pollen-associated lipid mediator expression.
the microbial community on pollen grains is not a static community but is affected by external environmental conditions.
pollen-associated microbes might be a potential source for allergenicity of airborne pollen.
